artifact: PHASE 3 / 6.01 DEPENDENCY-DELIVERY REMEDIATION §27 - required-dependency delivery is a property of the architecture, not of this document
corpusIsSynthetic: every corpus is generated from a parameterized shape: the defined-term names, the section numbers, the chain depth and the amounts are inputs. No real agreement, term, section, company or instrument appears in the file.

cases.question: does the same structure work under a DIFFERENT definition name?
cases.method: the bounding definition is renamed across three unrelated names; the whole composition must still be delivered

cases.question: does a cross-reference inside a required definition work for ANY section number?
cases.method: three unrelated section refs; each must be derived with CROSS_REFERENCE_IN_REQUIRED_DEFINITION and delivered

cases.question: is a FORWARDING definition's target delivered?
cases.method: two unrelated forwarding targets; the declaration and its target must both be required, the target evidenced as FORWARDING_DEFINITION_TARGET

cases.question: are several required definitions and a required section delivered together?
cases.method: the full closure must be delivered with no entry starved, every entry READ_ONLY_CONTEXT

cases.question: what happens when the closure does not fit?
cases.method: the ceiling is derived from the corpus's own measured closure (half, then a quarter), so the reaction is measured rather than a hard-coded trigger; re-sharding first, then water-filling, then an explicit certified planning failure

cases.question: can the required tier be rescued by, or leak into, the optional tier?
cases.method: no required key may appear in the interpretive tier at any ceiling

cases.question: does behaviour depend on VALUES?
cases.method: the same structure with different amounts must produce the identical required key set

cases.question: is an absent dependency fabricated?
cases.method: a cited section with no structural occurrence must be derived, disposed UNDELIVERABLE_DISCLOSED with empty text, and disclosed on the shard
